questions.q: Name the 4 compounds below. Spelling counts — use the accepted American spelling. Don't capitalize unless needed.
What is the correct formula for manganese(III) oxide?
questions.note: Mn³⁺ + O²⁻ — cross and drop: the 2 from O goes to Mn's subscript, the 3 from Mn goes to O's subscript → Mn₂O₃.

questions.q: If the ions, X⁺ and Y²⁻, form a neutral compound, how many total ions are required?
questions.note: X⁺ and Y²⁻ → X₂Y → 2 + 1 = 3 total ions.

questions.q: If the two ions, X³⁺ and Y⁻, form a neutral compound, how many total ions are required?
questions.note: X³⁺ and Y⁻ → XY₃ → 1 + 3 = 4 total ions.

questions.q: If the two ions, X⁴⁺ and Y²⁻, form a neutral compound, how many total ions are required?
questions.note: Cross and drop gives X₂Y₄ — but that's not the lowest ratio! Simplify to XY₂ → 1 + 2 = 3 total ions.

questions.q: Assume there are some new names and symbols for elements. If the ionic formula shown is By₃X, what would be the name? By = Byzantium (not a transition metal). X = Xuron.
questions.note: No roman numeral or prefix needed since By isn't a transition metal — the nonmetal X becomes the monatomic anion "xuride."

questions.q: What is the correct formula for magnesium hydrogen sulfite?
questions.note: Hydrogen sulfite (HSO₃⁻) is a polyatomic ion with a ‑1 charge. Magnesium is +2, so you need two HSO₃⁻ to balance.

questions.q: What is the correct formula for lithium hydrogen phosphate?
questions.note: Hydrogen phosphate is HPO₄²⁻ (‑2 charge), not "hydrogen" + "phosphate" separately. Lithium is +1, so you need two Li⁺ to balance.

questions.q: Name the 4 compounds below. Spelling counts — use the accepted American spelling. Don't capitalize unless needed.
What is the correct name for TiP?
questions.note: P³⁻ needs a +3 charge to balance, so it's titanium(III). Ionic names never use prefixes like "mono-."

questions.q: Name the 4 compounds below. Use capital 'I' in roman numerals (the letter that ends the word 'hi').
What is the correct formula for manganese(III) oxide?
What is the correct formula for ruthenium(II) phosphide?
questions.note: Ru²⁺ and P³⁻ — cross and drop gives Ru₃P₂ (already lowest terms).

questions.q: Name the 4 compounds below. Spelling counts — use the accepted American spelling.
What is the correct name for HBrO₂?
questions.given: Polyatomic ions: BrO₄⁻ = perbromate  ·  BrO₃⁻ = bromate  ·  BrO₂⁻ = bromite  ·  BrO⁻ = hypobromite
questions.note: BrO₂⁻ is bromite, and ‑ite polyatomic ions form ‑ous acids → bromous acid.

questions.q: Name the 4 compounds below. Don't include "(aq)" in the name.
How many H⁺ cations are necessary to form neutral acidic compounds with these polyatomic ions?
Which of the following is the best name for SeF₄?
Which of the following is the best name for P₂O₅?
questions.note: Both elements are nonmetals, so it's a covalent compound named entirely with prefixes — including "di-" on phosphorus, since there are 2 of them.

questions.q: Name the 4 compounds below.
Assume there are some new names and symbols for elements. If the ionic formula shown is AE₂, what would be the name? A = Adamantium (nonmetal). E = Exxon.
questions.note: Both A and E are nonmetals (covalent), and there's 1 A (no prefix on the first element when there's only one) and 2 E → "di-exxide."

questions.q: What is the correct order of decreasing size of the following ions?
questions.note: All four are isoelectronic (18 electrons) — with equal electrons, size is set by nuclear charge: fewer protons pulling on the same electron cloud means a bigger ion. P³⁻ (15 protons) > Cl⁻ (17) > K⁺ (19) > Ca²⁺ (20).
